source_text.lib/letflow/design/req237-zig-provenance: §2 defines the marker text (fixed literal: `PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):`) and the placement rule with FOUR citation-unit shapes as of the 2026-09-05 ISS-0510 amendment: (1) single citation line -- insert the marker on its own line immediately above a SOURCE:/CONTRACT SOURCE:-style line or lone bullet (and any hard-wrapped continuation lines of the same sentence); (2) paragraph -- for a .zig filename embedded in prose, the marker precedes the WHOLE paragraph (bounded by blank lines), not just the sentence/token; (3) table -- one marker above the table's header row, never per-row; (4) YAML comment-line/sequence-item (ISS-0510 addition, applies only inside YAML files) -- not expected to apply here since these 13 files are Markdown, not YAML, but check for embedded YAML code fences just in case. De-duplication: if a marker already immediately precedes a unit (grep -B1 check), do not insert a second one -- this makes the rule idempotent. §2(a) gives the exact regex: `PROVENANCE \(historical, not current decision authority\):` (also matches with plain `grep -F`). §4 gives two worked before/after examples showing the original path text is preserved byte-identical, only one new line added -- note the second worked example is specifically about a moduledoc/prose paragraph unit and about inserting the marker as the FIRST line inside a `@moduledoc """` body immediately after the opening `"""` when the citation is the module's opening paragraph; these 13 files are standalone .md design docs, not moduledocs, so the analogous case here is inserting the marker as the first line of the document/section if the citation paragraph is a document's or section's opening paragraph. §5 gives the verification method: (i) total-marked-count grep before/after must increase by exactly the number of citation units marked; (ii) `grep -c '\.zig' <file>` before/after must be EQUAL per file (no path text lost); (iii) idempotency -- re-running the pass a second time produces zero new markers. If a genuinely new citation-unit shape is found that does not match ANY of the four documented shapes (e.g. something specific to Markdown code-fence blocks, nested lists, or section headers unique to design-doc structure), do NOT invent a fifth ad-hoc convention: flag it as a new issue for CODE-DESIGNER (the same process ISS-0510 was raised through -- describe the shape, cite the file/line, and note it in this handoff's result.issues at MAJOR or MINOR per your judgement of how many citations it affects) and apply the CLOSEST-MATCHING existing shape in the meantime with a clear note in your result.summary, per REVIEWER's own established precedent this session for exactly this situation (ISS-0510).
